name: WeCare360
description: Online access to prescription medical cannabis for patients in Austria and Germany. People pick what they need help with, answer a short guided assessment and get matched with one or two suitable options. A doctor reviews the answers before anything can be prescribed.
highlights: Guided assessment for sleep, pain, stress and anxiety, and migraine
Answers matched to one or two suitable options
Medical review before any prescription is issued
German and English throughout, with customer accounts
tagline: A 60-second questionnaire that ends with a doctor's review, not a shopping cart.
overview: Most stores open with a catalogue. This one deliberately doesn't. The product is regulated, so the whole site is built around one guided path: choose a concern, answer the questions, see what fits, and let a doctor decide.
I worked across the Next.js front end and the Laravel API, so the assessment, the accounts, the bilingual content and the information pages all behave as one product.

steps.title: Pick a concern
steps.text: Four entry points, each with its own page and its own questions.

steps.title: Answer
steps.text: A short guided assessment that takes about 60 to 90 seconds.

steps.title: See the match
steps.text: One or two suitable options, with no confusing catalogue to dig through.

steps.title: Medical review
steps.text: A doctor reviews the answers, and delivery runs through a licensed pharmacy partner.

features: Condition pages for each concern area
Multi-step assessment and matching
Login and registration
How it works, costs, FAQ and contact pages
Legal pages: terms, privacy, cookies, imprint, shipping and refunds

name: 8killo
tagline: A one-page sales site up front, a full control center behind it.
description: Product store for the Israeli market. A one-page Hebrew sales site sells packages by length and dosage, and a custom admin runs everything after the click: orders, customers, shipping, stock, coupons and support.
overview: The public side is one focused sales page. The real work is behind it: a custom admin the team uses for daily operations, with sales and stock on a single dashboard.
Built with Next.js and a Laravel API, and deployed on a virtual host server using Nginx and Apache.
highlights: One-page Hebrew sales site priced in shekels
Admin dashboard for sales, orders and low-stock alerts
Harbiz app activation tracked per customer
Staff roles, permissions, activity log and login history
features: Orders, customers, payments and shipping, coupons
Products, packages and inventory by dosage
Site content, legal pages and FAQ editing
Live chat and customer messages
Reports, staff users, roles and permissions
hosting: Virtual host server with Nginx and Apache

name: Sanovida
description: Natural wellness store for Mexico, on the same foundation as 8killo. Customers buy products and programs, and the team runs orders, inventory, content and questionnaires from a custom admin.
highlights: Storefront for products and programs in Mexico
Questionnaires and quiz submissions in the admin
Inventory, packages and categories managed in-house
Sales reports and operational alerts on the dashboard
tagline: Same engine as 8killo, reshaped for a Spanish-speaking wellness brand.
overview: Sanovida and 8killo share an approach: a selling front end in Next.js and a Laravel API with a custom admin. What changes is the market, the language and the catalogue.
Here the admin adds programs, categories, questionnaires and quiz submissions on top of the usual orders and stock. It's deployed on a virtual host server using Nginx and Apache.
features: Orders, customers, payments and shipping, coupons
Products, packages, inventory, programs and categories
Website content, FAQ and app management
Questionnaires and quiz submissions
Messages, user accounts, roles and permissions
hosting: Virtual host server with Nginx and Apache

name: Rooté
description: Hair analysis platform and store for the US market. Visitors take a quiz, create an account or sign in with Google, and order from a brand-first storefront connected to a CRM through webhooks.
highlights: Hair analysis quiz with user accounts
Google sign in through NextAuth
CRM connected through webhooks
Ordering and delivery workflow
tagline: A hair analysis quiz that turns into a personal recommendation.
overview: The quiz is the front door, so it had to feel like part of the brand and not a form bolted on. Accounts and Google sign in keep each person's results attached to them.
Next.js and NextAuth on the front, a Laravel API behind, and Docker for deployment.

name: Shany Living
description: Furniture e-commerce store built for the Israeli market. A polished storefront backed by a Laravel API, with a full ordering and payment flow and a custom CMS so the team can manage products, content and orders on their own.
highlights: Ordering and online payment flow
Custom-built CMS for products and content
Refined, brand-led storefront UI
tagline: A furniture store the team can run without calling a developer.
overview: Furniture needs room to breathe, so the storefront is led by imagery and brand. Behind it, a custom CMS lets the team change products, content and orders on their own.

name: Rooted Performance
description: Performance and wellness brand in the US with an information management system and a custom CMS, built with Next.js on Supabase for auth, data and content.
highlights: Information management system
Custom CMS for editable content
Supabase-powered data and auth
tagline: A brand site with its own information system behind it.
overview: A public site and a private system in one project. Next.js handles both, and Supabase takes care of login, data and editable content.

name: RallyDVO
tagline: Built for a city that still has paddles out at 2 AM.
description: Pickleball hub for Davao City. Find a court from 74 venues, send a booking request, join an open play solo and log your score to climb the city leaderboard. Built with Next.js and SQLite, with venue data from a spreadsheet.
overview: RallyDVO puts pickleball in Davao City in one place: where to play, how late a court is open and what it costs per hour.
It's built with Next.js and SQLite, with venue details coming from spreadsheet data.
highlights: Directory of 74 venues with area and late-hours filters
Booking requests, plus a find-my-booking page
Open plays you can join solo
Weekly scoreboard and city leaderboard
features: Courts directory with a last-call board by closing time
Open play sessions
Results and leaderboard
Blog with guides on rates and etiquette
Sign in and account pages

name: Cabal Sea Saga Wiki
tagline: A wiki that does the math for your character build.
description: Wiki and build planner for Cabal Sea Saga. Look up skills, gear and systems for all nine classes, then plan a character: pick a class and focus, and the planner ranks the stats, fills in the build and adds up the totals. Next.js only, with all the computation in the app.
overview: The wiki puts class guides, game systems and a searchable database in one place, using values from the game client.

The build planner is the fun part. Choose a class, PvP or PvE and a damage type, and it works out what to prioritize across each game system and shows a build power score. You can save builds, compare two side by side, and share one with a build code. There's no back end: it's all Next.js and computation.
highlights: Build planner with PvE and PvP presets for each damage type
Stat totals and build power worked out live
Save builds, compare two, and share with a build code
Searchable database of skills, items, runes and titles
features: Class pages from Warrior to Dark Mage
Equipment, runes, medals, merit and mastery in one builder
Guides to Stellar Link, Myth Mastery, Honor Medal and more
Collections, achievements, trivia, themes and titles

name: UGLQ
description: Member portal for the United Grand Lodge of Queensland. A private login-protected platform with a report builder, a form builder and a full Masonic name builder, built with Next.js and Laravel.
tagline: Private tools for the members of a Queensland lodge.
overview: Everything sits behind a login, so the public screenshot is only the front door. Inside, members get tools built around how the lodge actually works.
highlights: Report builder
Form builder
Masonic name builder
Member login with structured workflows

name: ManpakBet
notice: A portfolio UI concept only. It isn't an operating casino or gambling service, and I don't intend to run one.
tagline: How far can a busy, game-heavy lobby go and still be easy to use?
description: UI portfolio piece: a game lobby concept in the style of popular Filipino gaming apps, built with Next.js and Laravel. Not an operating casino. It exists to show front-end work on a large, content-heavy interface.
overview: Gaming lobbies are a hard interface problem: thousands of tiles, many categories and a lot competing for attention. This one shows how I keep that much content easy to scan on a phone and on a wide screen.
It's a personal portfolio project, not a business. Nothing here is offered as a real gambling service.
highlights: Dense game grid with category and studio filters
Search across games and studios
Trending, editor's picks and new arrivals rows
Light and dark themes with mobile-first navigation
features: Home lobby with ranked rows
Category pages for each game type
Search and favorites
Account, wallet and support screens as UI only
